headline: Florida Attorney General Sues OpenAI and Sam Altman Personally Over FSU Shooting, First State to Do So
raw_snippet: Florida became the first US state to sue OpenAI when AG James Uthmeier filed a civil lawsuit also naming CEO Sam Altman personally. The complaint includes 10 counts — deceptive trade practices, negligence, product liability, fraudulent misrepresentation, and public nuisance. The case stems from the April 2025 FSU shooting where the gunman had approximately 16,000 ChatGPT interactions. A separate criminal investigation from April remains ongoing.

headline: Illinois Passes America's Strongest AI Safety Bill Requiring Annual Third-Party Audits of Frontier AI Companies
raw_snippet: Illinois legislature cleared SB 315, requiring frontier AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic to create, publish, and annually update safety risk plans, and to undergo mandatory annual independent third-party safety audits — the first such requirement in any US AI legislation. Both OpenAI and Anthropic publicly endorsed the bill, while a trade organization representing other AI companies opposed it.

headline: Sam Altman Reverses AI Jobs Apocalypse Warnings at Sydney Conference Days After IPO Filing
raw_snippet: At a Commonwealth Bank of Australia conference in Sydney on May 26, Sam Altman said he was 'delighted to be wrong' about AI eliminating entry-level white-collar jobs, admitting OpenAI's social and economic predictions were 'pretty wrong' while technological predictions were 'roughly right.' Critics note the mea culpa coincides with OpenAI's confidential S-1 filing on May 22, where a calmer jobs narrative benefits the public listing. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei separately predicted 10-20% unemployment from AI within 5 years.

headline: OpenAI Foundation Pledges $250 Million for AI-Disrupted Workers, First Major Initiative
raw_snippet: The OpenAI Foundation — which holds a 26% stake in OpenAI's for-profit business — announced its first major initiative: an initial $250 million commitment in grants, research partnerships, and programs to help workers and economies navigate AI-driven job displacement. The foundation plans to run some initiatives directly rather than just distributing grants. Tech industry layoffs in Q1 2026 hit nearly 80,000 positions with roughly half tied to AI efficiencies. First programs expected before end of 2026.

headline: OpenAI Frontier Governance Framework Maps Internal Safety Practices to California and EU AI Laws
raw_snippet: OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework on May 28, a regulatory translation layer mapping the company's Preparedness Framework to specific obligations under California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act and the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI. It covers CBRN risks, cyber offense, harmful manipulation, and loss-of-control scenarios. The EU AI Act's full transparency rules become enforceable August 2, 2026. Other frontier labs — Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI — are now implicitly expected to match this baseline.

headline: OpenAI Signs First Brazilian Media Deal with Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL, Settling 2025 Lawsuit
raw_snippet: On May 25, OpenAI announced a strategic content partnership with Brazil's Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL, its first media deal in Brazil. Journalism from Folha de S.Paulo and UOL will be integrated into ChatGPT with attribution and links. Brazil has 50+ million monthly active ChatGPT users processing ~140 million messages daily. The deal resolves a 2025 lawsuit filed by Folha demanding compensation for unauthorized content use. Partners also gain access to Codex, ChatGPT Enterprise, and API.

headline: OpenAI Outlines 2026 Midterm Election Safeguards: Live AP Vote Counts, Deepfake Watermarking, Cyber Defenses
raw_snippet: OpenAI readied its 2026 election safeguards ahead of US and Brazilian midterms. ChatGPT will show live vote counts from the Associated Press on election night. Democracy Works will provide voting and registration information. The plan has five planks: spreading reliable voting information, cybersecurity assistance, deepfake watermarking, enforcing election interference bans, and reducing political bias. OpenAI endorsed the Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act and Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act.

headline: Rosalind Biodefense Launched: OpenAI Opens GPT-Rosalind to Government and Vetted Developers
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched Rosalind Biodefense, sponsoring vetted developers' access to its gated GPT-Rosalind life-sciences model for pandemic preparedness and biosecurity. The company briefed the White House and federal agencies and is onboarding public-health-focused government partners. The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations is applying it to the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak response in DRC and Uganda.

headline: OpenAI and Thrive Holdings Announce Self-Improving Tax Agents Processing 7,000 Returns at 97% Accuracy
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Thrive Holdings co-developed a Codex-powered tax agent system that improved accuracy from 25% to 97% using real-world corrections as learning signals. The pilot through Crete Professional Alliance processed 7,000 1040 and 1041 filings, cutting preparation time by a third. OpenAI holds an equity stake in Thrive acquired in December 2025.

headline: Codex CLI v0.135.0 Shipped May 28 with Doctor Diagnostics, Completing Autonomous Agent Runtime Pivot
raw_snippet: Codex CLI v0.135.0 released May 28 with codex doctor diagnostics, Vim text objects, and cleaner tables. This follows v0.134.0 on May 26 which added conversation history search, --profile as canonical selector, and per-server MCP env targeting with OAuth for streamable HTTP. The four releases between April 23 and May 28 collectively transformed Codex from an interactive coding assistant into a persistent autonomous agent runtime.

headline: OpenAI Self-Serve Ad Platform Drops $50K Minimum, Opens ChatGPT Advertising to Small Businesses
raw_snippet: OpenAI expanded its ChatGPT advertising with conversion-focused ad formats, appointment-booking prompts, CPC bidding alongside CPM, and a new pixel plus Conversions API for server-side measurement. The self-serve Ads Manager beta, opened to all US businesses May 5, removed the previous $50,000 minimum. Ad business surpassed $100M ARR within 60 days of Feb 9 launch. OpenAI targets $2.5B in 2026 ad revenue, $100B by 2030.

headline: AI Regulation 2026 Fragments Into Three Simultaneous Fronts: CNN v Perplexity, DOJ Blocks Colorado Law, OpenAI EU Compliance
raw_snippet: As of May 31, AI regulation split into three simultaneous fronts: CNN filed a copyright lawsuit against Perplexity AI for scraping 17,000 news items, the DOJ blocked Colorado's AI law in a historic first federal challenge to state AI regulation, and OpenAI published its EU AI Act compliance framework. Bloomsbury Intelligence found that regulatory fragmentation prevents any single unified compliance program across EU, US state, and voluntary frameworks.

headline: OpenAI GPT-5.5-Cyber Granted to European Defenders Under Trusted Access Programme, George Osborne Leads Outreach
raw_snippet: OpenAI granted access to its GPT-5.5-Cyber model to dozens of European companies including Deutsche Telekom, BBVA, Telefonica, Sophos, and Scalable Capital under its Trusted Access for Cyber programme. George Osborne, head of OpenAI for Countries and former UK chancellor, presented the EU Commission with an action plan including model access and safety team briefings. Approved users must implement phishing-resistant authentication by June 1.

headline: OpenAI Announces o3 Retirement (Aug 26) and GPT-4.5 Retirement (Jun 27) from ChatGPT
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced model retirement dates: o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period, and GPT-4.5 will be retired from ChatGPT on June 27, 2026 following a 30-day sunset. These apply to ChatGPT only; API access continues. Canvas functionality was also removed from GPT-5.5 Instant and GPT-5.5 Thinking, replaced by writing blocks and code blocks in chat.

headline: Microsoft Build Conference Showcases Post-OpenAI AI Strategy with Homegrown Models
raw_snippet: Two months after Microsoft's 'conscious uncoupling' from OpenAI, Microsoft used Build to unveil homegrown AI models including a new coding model. The conference aimed to prove Microsoft can compete as an independent AI provider. Microsoft spent over $100 billion on its OpenAI partnership to date, per executive testimony on May 13 during the Musk v. Altman trial.

headline: OpenAI Files Confidential S-1, Eyes September IPO at Up to $1 Trillion Valuation
raw_snippet: OpenAI filed a confidential draft registration statement (S-1) with the SEC on May 22, targeting a public debut as early as September 2026 at an $850B-$1T valuation. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading. The filing follows the Musk lawsuit dismissal on May 18 which removed a significant legal overhang. Public S-1 will become available ~15 days before the roadshow. Q1 2026 revenue was $5.7B but operating margin was -122%, losing $1.22 per $1 earned.

headline: Pentagon Tests OpenAI and Google AI Models to Replace Anthropic After Defense Secretary Blacklisted It
raw_snippet: The Pentagon is testing AI models from OpenAI and Google with 25 'power users' to replace Anthropic's Claude, after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared Anthropic a supply-chain risk in March over its insistence on guardrails. OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon, and SpaceX are all cleared for classified IL6/IL7 defense networks. The evaluation ongoing through May further cements OpenAI's positioning as a defense contractor.

headline: Canadian Privacy Commissioners Find OpenAI Violated Privacy Laws in ChatGPT Training
raw_snippet: Canada's federal and provincial privacy commissioners released findings on May 6 that OpenAI violated Canadian privacy laws when training ChatGPT. The joint investigation found OpenAI's data collection was overly broad, including sensitive health and political data plus children's information, without valid consent for scraping publicly accessible personal information or using user interactions for model fine-tuning. OpenAI represented it has since implemented new mitigation measures.

headline: Musk Loses All Claims in OpenAI Lawsuit, Jury Deliberates Less Than Two Hours; Musk Vows Appeal
raw_snippet: A unanimous nine-member jury in Oakland dismissed all of Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and Sam Altman on May 18, finding the lawsuit was filed outside the three-year statute of limitations. The jury deliberated less than two hours. Musk called the verdict a 'calendar technicality' and confirmed he will appeal to the 9th Circuit. The dismissal removed a key legal overhang ahead of OpenAI's confidential S-1 filing four days later.

headline: Class Action Alleges OpenAI Shared ChatGPT User Data with Google and Meta via Tracking Pixels
raw_snippet: A federal class action (Couture v. OpenAI) filed May 13 in the Southern District of California alleges OpenAI embedded Meta's Facebook Pixel and Google Analytics in ChatGPT, sharing users' sensitive query topics, account identifiers, and email addresses without consent. The suit claims violations of the California Invasion of Privacy Act and Electronic Communications Privacy Act. The plaintiff demands statutory damages of $5,000 per violation.

headline: Sam Altman Offers Every Y Combinator Startup $2M in OpenAI Tokens for Equity, Total Value $338M
raw_snippet: At a May 20 Y Combinator event, Sam Altman offered $2 million in OpenAI API tokens to each of the 169 startups in the current batch in exchange for equity via uncapped SAFEs converting at Series A. The total implied value is ~$338 million at retail pricing. Critics like investor Jason Calacanis warn of a 'classic platform playbook' where OpenAI could analyze startup innovations to later offer similar features. OpenAI's marginal cost of running the compute is far below the retail credit price.

headline: OpenAI Q1 2026 Revenue Hits $5.7B but Operating Margin is Negative 122%, ChatGPT Growth Stalls
raw_snippet: OpenAI generated $5.7B in Q1 2026 revenue, nearly $1B more than Anthropic, boosted by Codex and enterprise sales. However, non-GAAP operating margin was -122%, meaning OpenAI lost $1.22 for every $1 of revenue (~$6.95B loss). ChatGPT weekly active users hit 920M in February but averaged 905M for the quarter, suggesting stalling growth. Paying customers rose from 47M to 55M. OpenAI projects $30B for full year 2026 but margins imply $36.6B+ in losses.

headline: Microsoft Spent Over $100 Billion on OpenAI Partnership, Executive Testifies at Musk Trial
raw_snippet: Microsoft deals executive Michael Wetter testified on May 13 that the company spent over $100 billion on its OpenAI partnership, including original investments, Azure infrastructure, and hosting costs through the current fiscal year ending June. CEO Satya Nadella separately testified he worried about Microsoft becoming 'the next IBM' in the relationship, revealing internal fears about over-dependence on OpenAI.

headline: OpenAI-Apple Partnership Frays, Legal Action Being Prepared Over Buried ChatGPT Integration
raw_snippet: Bloomberg reported May 14 that OpenAI is preparing possible legal action against Apple over the Siri ChatGPT integration announced at WWDC 2024. OpenAI expected the deal to funnel billions in new subscriptions, but claims the integration has been buried, features hard to find, and revenue far below projections. OpenAI has enlisted an outside law firm to explore options including a formal breach-of-contract notice.

headline: Florida AG's Criminal Investigation Into OpenAI Pushes Into 'Uncharted' Legal Territory
raw_snippet: Florida AG Uthmeier's criminal investigation into OpenAI over the FSU shooting continued into uncharted legal territory as of May 14. The AG acknowledged uncertainty about criminal liability, stating 'We are going to look at who knew what, designed what, or should have done what.' Investigators allege ~16,000 ChatGPT interactions by the shooter included advice on gun selection, ammunition, and optimal campus timing. A separate civil wrongful-death suit was filed May 11 by victim Tiru Chabba's widow.
